title: Al-Mutakabbir, the Supreme in Greatness
hook: the Supreme in Greatness, to whom alone greatness belongs, and one human family under it
tomorrow: she said yes. now how do you plan a life you can't see yet?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Jabbar: the Compeller who sets broken bones, and mend me, between two prostrations. He mends. The week's names come back in a moment.

The acceptance post is drafted: the logo, the confetti, a caption that sounds humble and isn't. Yesterday's question was what's left for pride once you see who mends what. Today's name answers. Al-Mutakabbir closes that list of names in Surah al-Hashr. Pickthall calls Him the Superb: the Supreme in Greatness, the one to whom greatness belongs.
screen: `A HUMBLE CAPTION THAT ISN'T.` → `WHAT'S LEFT FOR PRIDE?` → `AL-MUTAKABBIR.`

segments.voice: A sacred hadith, in Muslim's collection and Abu Dawud's, puts it as a picture, in paraphrase: greatness is My cloak. Whoever tries to wear it, I'll cast away. Then the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, defined pride so nobody could miss it, in Sahih Muslim: pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Not nice clothes; he said in the same breath that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Looking down on people. And in words from his farewell, recorded by Ahmad, in paraphrase: your Lord is one and your father is one. No Arab is above a non-Arab, no non-Arab above an Arab, no red above black, no black above red, except by mindfulness of God. One human family, and greatness belongs to none of it. That's this week, too: Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, Al-Mu'min, Al-Muhaymin, Al-'Aziz, Al-Jabbar, and now Al-Mutakabbir. Every one of them His. Something to tell a friend tonight: the Prophet's definition of pride doesn't mention clothes or money; it's about how you look at people.
screen: `GREATNESS IS HIS CLOAK.` · `PRIDE: LOOKING DOWN ON PEOPLE.` · `YOUR FATHER IS ONE.` · `A WEEK OF NAMES, ALL HIS.` · then, large: `GREATNESS IS HIS.`

segments.voice: Write by hand one thing you're proud of this week. Next to it, write the names of everyone who helped make it happen. For the sit, look at the list and let the credit spread out across it.
screen: `ONE THING YOU'RE PROUD OF.` · `EVERYONE WHO HELPED.`

segments.voice: Al-Mutakabbir: the Supreme in Greatness, to whom alone greatness belongs. Pickthall's word is the Superb.
Your line: greatness is his, and the rest of us stand level under it. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims say Allahu akbar, Allah is greater, at the start of each prayer and through it, and are taught to see humility toward people as part of faith.

fork.setup: you made the varsity team and a friend didn't. at lunch, people start joking about how badly he played. what does the Prophet's definition of pride say?
options: pride is looking down on people; skip the joke, and keep your joy.
pride is any happiness about winning; hide that you made the team.
it's only pride if you say it to his face, not behind his back.
fork.reveal: pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. joy in a good thing isn't it; the joke at his expense is.

chat.says: i said YES to Chicago 🎉 drafted a post that's 90% humblebrag. dadi read it over my shoulder. delete?
options: Keep the joy, cut the brag. Thank the people who got you there by name.
Delete it. Being proud of anything at all is the pride the hadith warns of.
Post it as is. It's not pride if everything in it is actually true.
chat.meaning: The Prophet defined pride as rejecting truth and looking down on people, not as joy. Greatness belongs to Allah; credit can be shared.
